answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, an agent economy can bind identities to multispectral reflectance telemetry. An agent authenticates by measuring optical reflectance of basalt rock on an open knoll, calibrated against chlorophyll absorption from a neighboring lotus pond. An attacker must deploy discrete spectrometer hardware per identity, incurring substantial equipment and site-access costs. However, shifting cloud cover alters ambient solar irradiance, occasionally triggering false rejections.
